title: Visual Jigsaw Post-Training Improves MLLMs
one_liner: Post-train a multimodal language model on a self-supervised ordering task over shuffled visual parts, so the model gets direct practice reconstructing visual structure without relying on text labels.
lead: Recent post-training for multimodal large language models often improves reasoning by supervising text outputs. The visual input is present, but it mostly serves as a source of sparse facts that later drive text generation. This paper argues that such post-training leaves visual understanding undertrained. Visual Jigsaw introduces a direct visual task instead. The model receives shuffled pieces of an image, a video, or a 3D scene and must output the correct ordering as text. The reward is automatically verifiable because there is a known correct permutation. This gives the model a vision-centric training signal without extra labels and without adding a visual generator. The task matters because reconstructing the right order forces the model to model local appearance, global structure, temporal continuity, or spatial arrangement, depending on the modality. Those are exactly the properties that many multimodal models use weakly when their post-training is dominated by text reasoning alone.

problem.h2: Text-centered post-training leaves visual structure underused
paras: A multimodal language model can answer questions about images, videos, and 3D scenes, but most post-training objectives still reward text behavior. The model may learn to explain, justify, or follow instructions better while making only limited gains in the actual representation of visual structure, because the loss checks the answer sentence more directly than the arrangement inside the visual input. That limitation shows up on tasks that depend on fine spatial detail, temporal order, or three-dimensional arrangement.

The issue is not that the model never sees visual inputs. The issue is that the training objective rarely forces it to reconstruct relationships inside those inputs. If the only rewarded outcome is a text answer, the model can often solve the task from a few extracted cues. It has little reason to build a strong model of how one patch relates to another patch, how one frame leads into the next, or how parts of a 3D observation fit together.

callout.html: Give the model a self-supervised task where success requires recovering the arrangement of shuffled visual pieces, because that trains visual structure directly and the reward can be checked exactly.

steps.text: Split an image into patches, a video into ordered segments, or a 3D input into structured parts.
Apply a random permutation so the original arrangement is hidden from the model.

steps.b: Ask for the order in language
steps.text: Prompt the model to output the correct permutation as a text sequence.
Compare the predicted permutation with the true one and compute a reward with no human labels.
Update the model so answers that reconstruct the visual arrangement become more likely.

paras: Visual Jigsaw changes the source of post-training supervision. Instead of asking the model mainly to produce better text about visual inputs, it asks the model to recover visual structure itself and uses the correctness of that recovery as the reward, which means the update now depends on whether the visual arrangement was understood.

hidden.name: How well the model knows which visual parts belong next to each other
paras: The paper is really training structural understanding. For an image, that means recognizing which patches complete the same object boundary or texture pattern. For a video, it means recognizing temporal continuity across frames. For 3D data, it means recognizing which observations are consistent with the same spatial arrangement. This knowledge is often present only weakly when training focuses on text outputs.

The jigsaw objective measures structural understanding directly. If the model cannot tell which patch should follow another or which frame comes earlier, it cannot recover the permutation. A correct permutation therefore implies that the model has captured relationships among parts rather than only isolated visual cues.

heat.caption: Darker means the model captures more of the relationships needed to rebuild the original arrangement.

reads.html: The model needs to know how the visual parts fit together, because predicting the correct order is impossible if it only recognizes isolated fragments.
The self-supervised permutation task exposes whether the model has learned local and global visual dependencies across images, videos, and 3D inputs.

mechanism.h2: Why the permutation task strengthens vision
paras: The jigsaw task removes the usual escape route where the model leans on text priors (common text patterns that can guide an answer without much visual analysis). The prompt does not ask for an open-ended description. It asks for a specific ordering that is determined by the visual arrangement alone. To answer correctly, the model must compare parts with one another and infer adjacency, continuity, or geometric compatibility.

This produces a dense training signal for visual structure. In a shuffled image, the model must use boundaries, repeated textures, and object shape continuity to find which patches belong together. In a shuffled video, it must use motion progression and state changes to reconstruct temporal order. In shuffled 3D observations, it must use viewpoint and spatial consistency to restore the arrangement. Because the reward is exact, the policy update can reinforce the specific decisions that helped recover those relations.

Expressing the permutation in natural language matters because it fits the existing multimodal language model interface. The model can stay architecturally unchanged while still receiving a vision-centric objective. That makes the method easy to apply in post-training and lets the learned visual improvements transfer to later language-conditioned tasks.

stages.s: Model learns stronger visual organization because correct rewards favor answers that reconstruct the input structure

math.words: The model is rewarded when the predicted permutation matches the true arrangement of the shuffled visual parts.
symbols: the reinforcement loss built from a verifiable reward
the permutation predicted by the model in text form
the true permutation that reconstructs the original visual arrangement

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose an image is split into four patches and then shuffled.
The model outputs an ordering of the four patch identifiers.
If the ordering reconstructs the original image, the reward is high because the model recovered the spatial structure correctly.
If two neighboring patches are swapped, the reward drops because the output breaks the original object boundaries or texture continuity.
Repeated training on this task strengthens the model's ability to reason about visual arrangement before any downstream question is asked.

math.note: The reward is self-supervised because the correct order comes from the shuffle operation itself, not from human annotation.

charts.title: Text-centered post-training
charts.note: The model improves on language behavior but still underuses many visual relations because post-training rarely tests them directly.

charts.title: Visual Jigsaw
charts.note: The self-supervised ordering task raises performance on several visual skills because each skill depends on reconstructing structure from shuffled parts.

items.html: If the partitioning scheme leaves obvious low-level cues, the model may solve the permutation without learning deeper structure because simple boundary matching is enough.
If too many parts are shuffled or the parts are too ambiguous, the reward becomes sparse because most predicted permutations are fully wrong. Then the post-training signal weakens.

A model may become good at ordering patches yet still struggle on tasks that require semantic interpretation beyond structure. The jigsaw task helps visual organization, but it does not replace domain-specific supervision because ordering alone does not teach every concept that a downstream task may require.
Choose partition schemes that require real structure recovery while keeping the reward informative. Then the task teaches reusable visual relations instead of superficial patch matching.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Post-train one multimodal model on a standard text-centered objective and another on the same objective plus Visual Jigsaw. Use one image dataset, one short video dataset, and one small 3D benchmark. For each modality, log jigsaw accuracy during post-training and then test downstream tasks that depend on structure, such as fine-grained visual comparison, temporal ordering questions, and viewpoint-consistent 3D reasoning. The demo should show that better permutation recovery during post-training leads to better downstream performance on tasks where visual arrangement matters, because both measurements depend on the same underlying ability to model how visual parts fit together.
demo.closing: The central claim to verify is that a self-supervised ordering task can improve visual understanding directly, even though the model expresses its answer in text, because the reward is determined by visual arrangement rather than by open-ended language quality.
